reports.title: 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results November 4, 2026 NYSE: CF

desk.headline: Sales up 12% to $1.86bn and EPS up 31% to $2.87, slightly below estimates; 2026 production and spending outlook given
results: Net sales rose 12% to $1.86bn on higher nitrogen prices and strong volumes, while natural gas costs were slightly lower.
Earnings per share rose to $2.87 from $2.19, helped by a lower share count (151.6m diluted shares vs 161.2m), but came in just under the $2.93 estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 25% to $833m; it included $62m of business-interruption insurance.
Ammonia plants ran at 97% of available capacity in the first nine months.
Over the past 12 months the company generated $2.0bn of free cash flow, after $306m of tax deposits in a US–Canada dispute.

guidance.summary: CF gives no earnings guidance. For 2026 it expects about 9.5m tons of gross ammonia production and about $950m of capital spending funded by CF.

points: Middle East urea exports are running near half of normal since hostilities began in February, keeping supply tight.
Close to 40% of European ammonia capacity is shut or cut back because of high gas prices.
Management expects firm nitrogen prices at least into the first half of 2027, with UAN orders booked into Q1 2027.
Yazoo City ammonia should restart in the first half of 2027; Blue Point stays on its $3.7bn budget for 2029.
CF bought back about 3m shares for about $367m in the quarter.
